pairs.evidence: app/_lib/task-maintenance.ts:79 The retention module keeps a private copy of the terminal statuses instead of deriving it from the one status definition. The function built on it (tasksToPrune) is only called by tests and disagrees with the store's real DELETE (`status NOT IN ('queued','running')`) on any status added later, so the tested mirror is not the code that runs.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/task-maintenance.ts:79 A consumer's own copy of the closed vocabulary, which is the use_when the technique names. It is test-only and drifts from the store predicate on any new status.
app/_lib/tasks.ts:576 The reaper writes its own honest state, interrupted, which is kept distinct from failed or succeeded. Progress callbacks are the first-tier signal.
app/_lib/tasks.ts:572 A live in-process handler outranks the expired budget. isTaskStale also never reaps a row with no start stamp (task-maintenance.ts:47).
app/_lib/tasks.ts:610 The DB row is the record of truth. Boot recovery marks running orphans interrupted and re-queues queued rows from the store before new work is pumped.

app/_lib/task-pump.ts:56 The slot cap is enforced at the one pump door with fair per-workspace selection. A queued entry is a durable 'queued' row, promotion runs on the same id, and a dedupe key stops two identical concurrent runs.

app/_lib/task-outcome-summary.ts:203 Batch outcomes report ok out of total plus a failure count, with per-item ok/code ledgers. Caveat: the task row's status is still 'succeeded' when every item failed.
app/_lib/task-poll-state.ts:64 A failed poll keeps the last good read and flags it, rather than substituting an empty 'nothing ran' state.
app/_lib/task-maintenance.ts:28 Handlers are code loops, not model-driven dispatcher loops. The 15-minute cap does sit above a 10-minute inner limit as a backstop.
app/_lib/tasks.ts:44 The executors run inside the control-plane process, so there is no separate executor plane.
app/_lib/tasks.ts:591 Tasks are bounded jobs with no session context to park. There is no parked state.
